# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: header version rendering tests (F1) — test-first ordering.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; version helper; no change to `packages/herdr/package.json` (version source only).

# Implement: Remove mode-switch machinery, serial Phase 2

Remove the client half of the retired fast/cheap operating mode and fix audit Phase-2 parallelism to serial (parent WL-0MVE1NZ4J000H5NH, AC1/AC5).

## Goal
Herdr no longer contains or configures a mode-switch worker, sends no `/admin/set-mode` calls, exposes no `modeSwitch*` settings, and always runs audit Phase 2 serially; the plugin starts and dispatches normally.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts`, `mode-switch-worker.test.ts`, `mode-switch-integration.test.ts` and `drain-regression-guard.test.ts` are deleted.
- [ ] The `modeSwitchEnabled`, `modeSwitchIdleThresholdMs` and `modeSwitchPollIntervalMs` settings (types, defaults, parsing, clamping, validation) are removed from `settings.ts`; existing settings files containing those keys still load (keys ignored, no migration).
- [ ] The `mode-switch` scheduler task and its worker/poll-interval options/imports are removed from `worklist.ts`.
- [ ] `index.ts` no longer constructs or holds the worker, wires `onProxyIdle`/`onOperatorCommand`, or passes an observed `mode` to the downtime dispatcher; every `/admin/set-mode` call is gone.
- [ ] `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` is always `'1'`; `DowntimeSpawnConfig` and its `mode`/`slotBudget`/`freeSlots`/`concurrentDispatchCap` plumbing are deleted while the existing free-slot dispatch gating is unchanged.
- [ ] The package builds, the changed-scope tests (including the F3 backward-compatibility specs) pass, and the plugin starts and dispatches in an existing dispatch test.

## Minimal Implementation
1. Delete the four worker/test files.
2. Strip `modeSwitch*` from `settings.ts` defaults/parse/validation; keep permissive loading of unknown keys.
3. Remove the `mode-switch` scheduler task and options from `worklist.ts`.
4. Remove worker construction, holder, callbacks and mode passing from `index.ts`.
5. Collapse `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` to a constant `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM: '1'` and delete `DowntimeSpawnConfig` and its call-site plumbing in `downtime-worker.ts`.

## Key Files
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.ts` (delete)
- `packages/herdr/src/mode-switch-worker.test.ts`, `mode-switch-integration.test.ts`, `drain-regression-guard.test.ts` (delete)
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts`, `settings.test.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`

# Implement: Pi Worklog extension injects X-Priority

Add the Worklog pi extension module that conveys pane-launch request priority to the LLM proxy (parent WL-0MVE1NZ4J000H5NH, AC4).

## Goal
Every pi session herdr launches reads `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` and, when it is a valid priority, sets the `X-Priority` header on every provider request; otherwise it leaves headers untouched.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] New `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/request-priority.ts` validates `process.env.HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY`, accepting only `low`, `medium`, `high`, and sets the `X-Priority` request header via a `before_provider_headers` hook.
- [ ] Unset, empty or invalid values leave the header map untouched (no assumed default).
- [ ] The module is registered from `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/index.ts`.
- [ ] The F2 unit tests (valid/invalid/unset) pass; no proxy (`llm-manager`) change is made.

## Minimal Implementation
1. Add a small `resolveRequestPriority(env)` helper returning `low|medium|high|undefined`.
2. Register `before_provider_headers(ctx => ({...headers, ...(prio ? {'X-Priority': prio} : {})}))`.
3. Export/register the module from `index.ts`.
4. Rely on the proxy's own `medium` default when no header is sent.

## Key Files
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/request-priority.ts` (new)
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/index.ts`
- `packages/tui/extensions/Worklog/request-priority.test.ts`

# Implement: herdr interactive dispatch priority

Resolve the dispatched work item's priority at interactive dispatch time and thread it to the pane/headless process as `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` (parent WL-0MVE1NZ4J000H5NH, AC2).

## Goal
Interactive agent panes and headless `spawnBackgroundPi` runs carry the mapped request priority of the work item they were dispatched for, so the proxy can serve urgent work responsively.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] New `packages/herdr/src/request-priority.ts` exposes the interactive mapping (`low`→`medium`, `medium`/`high`/`critical`→`high`, unresolved→`high`) and the downtime mapping (`low`/`medium`/`high` unchanged, `critical`→`high`, unknown→`medium`) as pure, unit-tested helpers.
- [ ] `index.ts` resolves the dispatched item's work-item priority from the worklist item cache, falling back to a fail-open `wl show` lookup; a free-form `/prompt:`, missing id, lookup failure or timeout maps to `high` and still dispatches.
- [ ] Interactive agent panes and headless `spawnBackgroundPi` runs set `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` in the child env from the mapped priority.
- [ ] `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` forwards the request priority into the spawned pane process (e.g. `exec env HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY=… bash run-pi-agent.sh …`, or `grid.py`/`pane split --env` passthrough on the resize path), with usage docs updated.
- [ ] `packages/herdr/scripts/run-in-pane.sh` either mirrors the passthrough or documents that shell-command panes carry no priority context.
- [ ] The F1 mapping and dispatch tests pass.

## Minimal Implementation
1. Add the mapping helpers and unit-test them (F1 specs).
2. At the interactive dispatch seam, read the item's priority from the cached worklist item; else `wl show <id> --json` with a short timeout; default `high`.
3. Add `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` to the child env for panes and `spawnBackgroundPi`.
4. Update `send-to-pi.sh` (and `grid.py` if the resize path is used) to preserve the variable into the pane process.
5. Reuse `scrubRepositoryOverrides`-style env construction so the variable survives the launch.

## Key Files
- `packages/herdr/src/request-priority.ts` (new)
- `packages/herdr/src/index.ts`
- `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh`
- `packages/herdr/shared/grid.py`
- `packages/herdr/scripts/run-in-pane.sh`
- `packages/herdr/src/request-priority.test.ts`

# Implement: downtime dispatch priority

Carry each downtime-dispatched item's priority to the proxy as `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` (parent WL-0MVE1NZ4J000H5NH, AC3).

## Goal
Unattended downtime work is served at a priority derived from the selected candidate, so high/critical work outranks background work and low-priority work is cheap and polite.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` (or its successor) sets `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` from the selected `DowntimeCandidate.priority` using the downtime table (`low`→`low`, `medium`→`medium`, `high`→`high`, `critical`→`high`, unknown/absent→`medium`).
- [ ] The selected candidate's priority is plumbed to the spawn options for every downtime tier (audit, pane, implement); a missing priority falls open to `medium`.
- [ ] `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM` remains constant `'1'`.
- [ ] The F3 downtime tests pass and no `llm-manager` change is made.

## Minimal Implementation
1. Pass the resolved mapped priority through the spawn options at each dispatch seam.
2. Add `HERDR_REQUEST_PRIORITY` to the spawn env beside `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD`.
3. Keep `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM: '1'` and the existing free-slot gating untouched.

## Key Files
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts`
- `packages/herdr/src/request-priority.ts`
- downtime-worker tests

# Audit-batch dispatch — test specs (test-first)

Test-first companion to WL-0MVEDM8OT007WDRS. Write the FAILING test specs for depth-aware audit batching BEFORE any implementation. The specs pin the behaviours in parent AC1–AC5 so the implementation items (WL-0MVEDM8OT007WDRS children C3–C5) verify against them.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Covers parent AC6: Test coverage in the herdr package: shallow depth keeps the single-dispatch idle reset; depth at or above `browseItemCount` with `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX = N` yields N sequential audits in one idle window; idle gates, the active-audit marker, the cap, the depth drop and dispatched-marker exclusion are asserted.

- `downtime-worker.settings.test.ts`: `clampDowntimeAuditBatchMax` clamps to [1, 5], non-finite falls back to the default (2), `1` = legacy/off; `loadSettings` parses `downtimeAuditBatchMax` from a fixture config (valid, invalid, missing).
- `downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts` (parent AC6a): shallow depth (< `browseItemCount`) keeps today's single-dispatch behaviour — exactly one dispatch and a full idle-tracker reset (`tracker.record(false)` / `perSlotTracker.record([])`) after it, and no `audit-batch-continue` token.
- `downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts` (AC6b): depth ≥ `browseItemCount` with `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX = N` produces exactly N sequential audit dispatches within one idle window, each continuation gated by a fresh per-tick idle/slot/contention re-check.
- `downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts` (AC6c): an unsatisfied idle-duration gate and sub-2 free slots block ALL dispatch including continuations; `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2` is never relaxed.
- `downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts` (AC6d): a non-stale host-wide/per-worklog active-audit marker blocks a concurrent continuation; the continuation proceeds only after the marker is released.
- `downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts` / `coordination-dispatch.test.ts` (AC6e, AC6f, AC4): the cap and the depth-drop end the batch and restore single-dispatch behaviour; dispatched-marker exclusion prevents the same item being selected twice; a failed CAS claim / spawn failure / any non-`dispatched` outcome ends the batch; in coordination mode the leader defers the own-backlog leadership hand-off until batch end.
- Every spec is runnable against the current tree (red) — each uses only the current public API (dispatch functions, worker object, settings loaders) and existing fixture/stub patterns.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `describe`/`it` blocks to the five test files in the parent's Key Files using the existing mock-deps / `createDowntimeWorker` / `dispatchDowntimeWork` / `dispatchFromCoordination` patterns.
- Assert on dispatch outcome (`dispatched`, `kind`, `reason`), the idle tracker state, the decision-log entries (tokens + metadata), and leadership state (`isLeader`) — never on wall-clock timing.
- Run the herdr package suite via the test skill to confirm the new specs fail as expected against the current tree.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts
- packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.settings.test.ts

## Dependencies

- None (test-first — the implementation items depend on this spec).

## Deliverables

# Depth-derived batch activation + conditional idle reset in `tick()`

Core of parent AC1/AC2/AC3: compute the audit-eligible depth from the already-fetched Herdr head, activate a bounded batch budget only when the queue is deep, and replace the unconditional post-dispatch idle reset with a conditional one scoped strictly to an audit-batch continuation.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Covers parent AC1: Depth-aware batching: an audit-eligible depth at or above `browseItemCount` with `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX` above 1 allows distinct audit continuations inside one idle window until the cap or the depth drop.
- Covers parent AC2: Sequential single-audit safety: every continuation re-checks the idle-duration gate, `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2`, proxy contention, code freeze, the active-audit markers and single-flight — no gate is relaxed, only the post-dispatch idle reset is deferred.
- Covers parent AC3: No duplicate or re-dispatched items: each continuation selects a distinct item through the existing classification and dispatched-marker exclusions, and any non-`dispatched` outcome ends the batch.

- **Depth computation (AC1).** A helper derives the audit-eligible depth from the already-fetched Herdr head: count items where `classifyItemForDispatch(item, now) === 'audit'` (root `completed`/`in_review`, excluding fresh-audited, producer-review, assignee-held and soft-deleted items). No new `wl` subprocess is added to the common dispatch path.
- **Activation rule (AC1).** Batch mode is active only when `depth >= browseItemCount` AND `auditBatchMax > 1`; otherwise behaviour is byte-for-byte today's: one dispatch per idle window followed by a full idle-tracker reset.
- **Batch budget state (AC1/AC3).** An in-memory per-worker budget (like `lastDispatchAt`/`cooldownUntil`) counts audit dispatches in the current batch, is initialised to `auditBatchMax` when a batch activates, and is cleared when: the cap is reached, the depth drops below the threshold, a non-audit dispatch occurs, an audit dispatch ends in any non-`dispatched` outcome (including `claim-failed`, `claim-rolled-back`, `spawn-failed`, `marker-write-failed`, `anchor-unavailable`), the worker pauses/cooldowns, or leadership is lost.
- **Conditional idle reset (AC2).** On a successful **audit** dispatch while a batch is active with budget remaining, `tick()` does NOT call `tracker.record(false)` / `perSlotTracker.record([])`; for every other dispatch, or when the budget/threshold no longer applies, today's reset is preserved exactly. Every gate (idle-duration threshold, `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2`, `slotOwned`, `contention_queue_depth == 0`, code-freeze, host-wide/per-worklog audit markers, single-flight) is still re-checked on every tick, including continuations — no gate is relaxed or bypassed.
- **No duplicate / no target skipping (AC3).** Continuations flow through the existing classification and dispatched-marker exclusions (audit id-guard, staleness-aware release, attempt budget, freshness/recency). A continuation never skips to a different target after a failed outcome — the batch simply ends.
- **Regression safety.** Non-audit dispatch (critical/implement/plan/intake/risk-effort) still resets the tracker and never arms a batch even when the queue is deep; legacy mode (no `coordinationDir`) keeps its existing tier-chain semantics.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `computeAuditEligibleDepth(items, now)` (or equivalent) beside `readReviewQueueGate` in `downtime-worker.ts`; reuse `classifyItemForDispatch` — no second eligibility definition.
- Add `auditBatch` worker-scope state (cap, remaining, active flag) and a `shouldDeferIdleReset(outcome, depth, cap)` decision helper (pure, exported for tests).
- In `tick()`: after a successful dispatch, look at `outcome.kind === 'audit'`, the current depth and the remaining budget, then conditionally skip the reset; clear the budget on every batch-ending condition listed in AC3.
- Extend `DowntimeDispatchOutcome` with the minimal machine-readable surface the worker needs (e.g. `auditBatchEligible?: boolean`), documented in the interface comment.
- Cover with the specs from C1 plus any new unit tests for the pure helpers.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.dispatch.test.ts
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts

## Dependencies

- Depends on the settings/plumbing item (C2) for `auditBatchMax`.

## Deliverables

- Depth helper + batch budget + conditional reset, with green audit-tier/dispatch/orchestrator tests.
data.title: Depth-derived batch activation + conditional idle reset

# Coordination-mode batch continuation + deferred leadership hand-off

Parent AC4: on the production coordination path the leader must source continuation audit targets from its own Herdr head (bounded window extension, same ranking) without releasing leadership mid-batch, and defer the own-backlog leadership hand-off until the batch ends.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Covers parent AC2: Sequential single-audit safety: every continuation re-checks the idle-duration gate, `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2`, proxy contention, code freeze, the active-audit markers and single-flight — no gate is relaxed, only the post-dispatch idle reset is deferred.
- Covers parent AC3: No duplicate or re-dispatched items: each continuation selects a distinct item through the existing classification and dispatched-marker exclusions, and any non-`dispatched` outcome ends the batch.
- Covers parent AC4: Coordination-mode compatibility: the leader sources continuation targets from its own Herdr head without releasing leadership mid-batch, and hands off leadership once at batch end.

- **Continuation source (AC4).** After a successful batch-eligible audit dispatch, `dispatchFromCoordination` may dispatch the next audit target from the leader's own head extension (`getHerdrListHead` + `fetchExtendedHerdrItems`, `includeNonCritical` filter as today) instead of only after total offer-list exhaustion — still exactly one dispatch per invocation, never two.
- **Same filters (AC3/AC4).** Every own-head continuation passes the identical sequential filters as the existing own-backlog fallback: `classifyItemForDispatch`, dispatched-marker exclusion (id-guard + staleness), attempt budget, non-terminal cooldown, code-freeze, audit slot minimum (≥2), in-flight critical guard, review-queue hold for implements. The continuation selects only `audit`-kind items.
- **No duplicate target (AC3).** The item just dispatched, and any item already dispatched in this batch, is never re-selected in the same batch — enforced by the existing marker exclusion plus an explicit batch-local exclusion set, covered by a test.
- **Leadership timing (AC4).** An own-backlog (`ownBacklogDispatch === true`) audit dispatch during an active batch with budget remaining does NOT trigger `releaseLeadership()` in that tick; the step-down happens exactly once at batch end (cap reached, depth dropped, failed continuation, or the next tick when the batch is no longer active). A normal in-view dispatch is unchanged.
- **No regression.** Non-batch coordination dispatch, leader election/lease TTL, coordination check-ins, pruning and the offer path are unchanged; `dispatchFromCoordination` direct-API callers without `freeSlots`/`auditBatchMax` keep today's behaviour (fail-open).

## Minimal Implementation

- Thread `auditBatchMax` and the batch-continuation intent through `dispatchFromCoordination`'s options (a boolean/marker set by `tick()` when the batch is active, plus the dispatched-target set for the current batch).
- Factor the existing own-backlog candidate loop into a reusable helper so the continuation path applies the exact same filters (no duplicated filter chain).
- Add `auditBatchContinuation?: boolean` (and any needed batch metadata) to `DowntimeDispatchOutcome`, documented, so `tick()` can decide the leadership step-down and the idle-reset deferral without re-deriving state.
- In `tick()`, gate the existing `outcome.ownBacklogDispatch === true` step-down on batch-inactive (deferring it to batch end).
- Cover with the coordination-dispatch and orchestrator specs from C1.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts
- packages/herdr/src/coordination-dispatch.test.ts
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.orchestrator.test.ts

## Dependencies

- Depends on the depth/reset item (C3) for the batch state and outcome surface.
- Depends on the observability item (C5) for the continuation token contract.

## Deliverables

- Leader own-head continuation with unchanged filter semantics and deferred step-down, with green coordination-dispatch/orchestrator tests.
data.title: Coordination batch continuation + deferred leadership hand-off

# Observability: audit-batch decision tokens and metadata

Parent AC5: every batch decision is recorded in the existing downtime decision log at the existing rate limit. Existing reason tokens are unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Covers parent AC5: Observability: every batch decision is recorded in the downtime decision log with a distinct reason token (`audit-batch-continue` and the existing held/blocked tokens) including depth, cap and remaining; rate limiting is unchanged.

- **Continuation token (AC5).** An accepted audit-batch continuation records a distinct token (e.g. `audit-batch-continue`) in the existing decision log with metadata: `depth`, `cap`, `remaining`, plus today's standard fields (`freeSlots`, `totalSlots`, `ownerPresent`, `runningPanes`, `contentionDepth`).
- **Blocked continuation tokens (AC5).** Held/blocked continuations reuse the existing tokens unchanged — `audit-in-flight` (per-worklog single-flight) and `audit-host-saturated` (host-wide marker) for marker blocks, `slot-owned`, `proxy-contention`, `code-freeze`, `review-queue-hold`, `no-candidate` — with the batch metadata (depth/cap/remaining) attached when a batch was active.
- **Batch end observability.** Batch deactivation transitions that would otherwise be silent surface in the decision log where a distinct signal adds value (e.g. cap reached / depth dropped) without spamming the log — still rate-limited by `DOWNTIME_DECISION_LOG_MIN_INTERVAL_MS`.
- **Rate limiting + header unchanged.** The header blocking token updates on every refusal exactly as today; `DOWNTIME_DECISION_LOG_MIN_INTERVAL_MS` behaviour is preserved for refusals; no existing reason-token test regresses.
- **Doc alignment.** The new/attached tokens match the token list committed in the docs item (C6).

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend the decision-log entry shape (`CoordinationLogEntry` kind `decision`) with optional `batch?: { depth: number; cap: number; remaining: number }` + the `audit-batch-continue`/`audit-batch-held`(if distinct signal) reasons routed through the worker's `recordDecision`.
- Emit the continuation token from `tick()` after a batch-armed continuation attempt (accepted or held) with the live depth/cap/remaining; re-compute depth from the head the same way as C3.
- Update the reason-token comment blocks in `downtime-worker.ts` and the dispatcher doc token list (§~60/108).
- Cover with the decision-log specs from C1 (`downtime-log.test.ts`).

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-log.test.ts
- docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md (token list)

## Dependencies

- Depends on the depth/reset item (C3) for the batch state and depth computation.

## Deliverables

- Observable batch decisions (token + depth/cap/remaining metadata) with green token/metadata specs.

# Documentation: batch setting, activation rule, sequential-safety invariants and decision tokens

Parent AC7: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` and the settings reference document the new setting, its activation rule, the sequential safety invariants and the new decision tokens. All related documentation (incl. code comments) is updated and consistent with shipped behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Covers parent AC7: Documentation: `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` and the settings reference document the new setting, the activation rule, the sequential safety invariants and the new decision tokens.

- **Dispatcher doc.** `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md` documents:
   - the setting (`downtimeAuditBatchMax`, default 2, clamped 1–5, `1` = legacy/off) — in the settings table (~§1638) and the configuration prose;
   - the activation rule (audit-eligible depth ≥ `browseItemCount` from the Herdr head + `auditBatchMax > 1`);
   - the sequential single-audit safety invariants (AC2 gate list — nothing relaxed, only the post-dispatch idle reset deferred);
   - the new decision tokens (`audit-batch-continue` and held/blocked variants) in the reason-token lists (~§60/108) and observations section;
   - the deferred own-backlog leadership hand-off (WL-0MUU4XFU90008E24 interplay).
- **README.** `packages/herdr/README.md` adds an operator-facing bullet for `downtimeAuditBatchMax` in the settings list (~§521) and notes the batching behaviour (sequentially within one idle window, at most one active audit) in the audit-dispatch section.
- **Code comments.** Comments in `downtime-worker.ts` / `settings.ts` / `index.ts` describing the batch mode, its lifecycle and trade-offs (incl. the proxy-busy caveat: the audit pane's own occupancy still resets the tracker; the deferred reset is only the dispatcher's own post-dispatch reset) match the shipped behaviour in C3–C5.
- **Consistency.** Every documented token, setting name and activation rule matches the implementation; a doc-consistency scan (C7) finds no stale single-dispatch-only claims.

## Minimal Implementation

- Edit the three doc targets and the code comments touched by C3–C5; cross-check reason-token lists, the settings table and the host-wide serialisation section (§1044).
- Verify the AC7 checklist against the shipped behaviour via the verification item (C7).

## Key Files

- docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md
- packages/herdr/README.md
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts (comment blocks)

## Dependencies

- Depends on the implementation items C3, C4, C5 having landed.

## Deliverables

- Updated dispatcher doc, herdr README and code comments, consistent with the shipped behaviour.
data.title: Docs: audit batching setting, invariants and decision tokens

# Verification: full suite + documentation consistency (parent AC8)

Final verification slice for WL-0MVEDM8OT007WDRS. Confirms the full suite passes with the new changes and that all docs are consistent with the shipped behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Covers parent AC6: Test coverage in the herdr package: shallow depth keeps the single-dispatch idle reset; depth at or above `browseItemCount` with `DOWNTIME_AUDIT_BATCH_MAX = N` yields N sequential audits in one idle window; idle gates, the active-audit marker, the cap, the depth drop and dispatched-marker exclusion are asserted.
- Covers parent AC8: Full suite: the full project test suite passes with the new changes, at minimum the full herdr package suite.

- **Full suite (AC8).** The full project test suite passes with the new changes — at minimum the full herdr package suite — run via the test skill; a red tree is never pushed (build → test → commit order).
- **Doc consistency (AC7).** A scan of `docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md`, `packages/herdr/README.md` and the settings reference finds no stale references to single-dispatch-only behaviour and no contradiction with the shipped batch mode.
- **AC traceability.** Parent AC1–AC7 each trace to a green spec/behaviour; any gap is recorded in a comment on WL-0MVEDM8OT007WDRS.
- **Commit hygiene.** The commit message references the parent work item; the changed-scope test gate passes before commit.

## Minimal Implementation

- Run the test skill (full changed-scope suite) once per the shared background-job etiquette; triage any gate-reported failures via the triage skill.
- Cross-check the parent AC list against the spec/test names in `downtime-worker.audit-tier.test.ts`, `coordination-dispatch.test.ts` and the doc changes.
- Add a completion comment on WL-0MVEDM8OT007WDRS summarising the verification result and commit hash.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/ (full herdr suite)
- docs/dev/downtime-dispatcher.md

## Dependencies

- Depends on C1–C6 being committed.

## Deliverables

- Green full suite, doc-consistency sign-off, AC traceability comment on the parent.
